events.text: there is a cube on the the table, solve the cube. proceed until the task is solved, save all the images to the file system you read from the camera. prioritize task efficiency, avoid unnecessary checks and preflights. the cube is definitely solvable, you should work hard to gather information and solve the cube.
The sticker state is resolved, and the solver found a four-turn solution: `R U' F R'`. I’m now arranging the grasps to execute those turns.
Three turns are verified. One turn remains; I’ve switched to the equivalent `B D'` finish to avoid a wrist-limit problem.

device_map.description: Two YAM arms mounted 0.6096 m apart on a bench, two flange-mounted RGB-D cameras and a fixed overhead camera. Static illustrative pose, not calibrated/live kinematics.
device_map.highlight_note: Exact device IDs from selected original tool arguments. Cameras embedded in cube_capture helper results are indicated in the observation cards.

source_review.camera_motion: Fixed external camera; end on the solved cube with blue face up, before the later lowering and placement.
source_review.human_interventions: No intervention visible in reviewed samples. Later operator confirmation is outside this edit.

source_review.outcome: Final layer turn produces uniform faces; whole-cube presentation shows the blue face up. Stop here at user request.
source_review.pacing: All successful physical command windows include 0.9 s guards and run at no more than 20x, with at least 0.4 s per motion; key quarter turns and final presentation run at 5x. Stationary intervals use continuous linear speed ramps. Final result holds for 2.2 s.

elapsed_time.clock: Original recording time, using the same continuous source map as the footage; not the 75-second export clock.
elapsed_time.total_definition: Retained recording from frame zero through the solved blue-face-up presentation; later placement footage is excluded.
